effect: Connecting the balance pathways to the body completed the goal and showed how they help steady vision and adjust posture alongside other sensory information.
reaction: The opposite eye movement was a satisfying, concrete outcome of the construction.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the completed pathways to the body was most worthwhile: the planned turning-head views make the link between balance signals, stable vision and posture tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate nerve and reflex-pathway fittings were fairly straightforward and repetitive, though they made the route to both targets clear.

surprise.text: The weighted-membrane comparison clarified that the organs respond to changes in straight-line motion, not steady motion.

arbitrary.text: Trying to connect the rotation sensors directly to the nerve pathways failed because the two organ types first had to be combined. That ordering was not obvious, although the feedback automatically completed the assembly.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the final reflex example connected the anatomy to an observable action, though the intermediate fittings were less engaging.
